etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English fulminaten, borrowed from Latin fulminātus, perfect passive participle of fulminō (“to lighten, hurl or strike with lightning”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from fulmen (“lightning which strikes and sets on fire, thunderbolt”), from earlier *fulgmen, *fulgimen, from fulgeō, fulgō (“flash, lighten”). Doublet of fulmine. More at fulgent.
senses: (intransitive, figuratively) To make a verbal attack.
(transitive, figuratively) To issue as a denunciation.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From fulminic acid +‎ -ate (“salt or ester”). By surface analysis, fulmine +‎ -ate.
senses: (chemistry) Any salt or ester of fulminic acid, mostly explosive.
